Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · School & learning

teacher noun

also schoolteacher, schoolmaster, Latin teacher, instructor, teachers’ room, staff room, teaching assistant

classical

Traupman 32, 169, 391
Traupman 338

magister, magistrī m.; magistra, magistrae f.

Declension on Wiktionary

Other words

  • lūdī magister — schoolmaster

    also used · classical · M-O s.v. teacher; Cic.

  • praeceptor, praeceptōris m. — instructor, teacher

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 4.7.96: praeceptor tuus, quī tē hanc fallāciam docuit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 30; Traupman 333 · Declension on Wiktionary

    The one who gives rules (praecepta): a teacher of an art or of conduct.

  • docēns, docentis m./f. — a teacher (the one teaching)

    present participle of doceō used as a noun · also used · modern · Traupman 28, 30 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Traupman’s word; Lewis & Short do not list the participle as a noun, so magister is the plain word.

Examples

  • Quid hodiē magistra vōs docuit?

    What did the teacher teach you today?composed

  • oecus magistrōrum (magistrārum)

    the teachers’ room, the staff roomTraupman 391

  • magistrae (magistrī) adjūtor (adjūtrīx)

    a teaching assistantTraupman 391

See also primary teacher, school.
